# count-structure-fixtures.txt — labeled expected-match set for Check 62
#
# PROVENANCE. The FLAG/CLEAN pair below is the two-armed fixture handed over by the
# probe-validity card at core/hooks/testdata/count-structure-fixtures.txt. That file
# is authoritative for the pair's SEMANTICS and is not modified here. Its two arms are
# written as INLINE enumerations (`preamble: item; item; …`), a structure form Check 62
# v1 deliberately does not examine — so the arms are restated here in the block form
# the shipped predicate reads, preserving both discriminating properties:
#   (a) the numeral counts SHAPES while the enumeration lists CLASSES, so the units are
#       not comparable and the FLAG arm's mismatch is real; and
#   (b) the corrected twin's per-item parenthetical counts sum to the stated total, so
#       it reconciles under the sub-count reading as well as the identity reading.
# The verbatim inline originals ship below as SCOPE-OUT cases, which makes the v1
# coverage boundary a committed, testable fact rather than a sentence in a design doc —
# and gives the inline-form graduation its regression set already written.
#
# WHY THIS PAIR IS LOAD-BEARING — read before tuning the predicate against it.
# An earlier candidate scored 8 false positives instead of 51 (six times better) and
# was ready to ship on the numbers alone. This pair falsified it twice over. Its
# terminal-window rule left the FLAG arm unexaminable — 0 pairs, 0 flags, reported as
# "clean" — a BROKEN sensitivity arm. Its preposition suppressor discarded `across 6
# classes`, the very cardinal that RECONCILES the CLEAN arm, turning the specificity
# arm into a false alarm. A probe that examines almost nothing scores beautifully on
# false positives and proves nothing. Both rules were deleted. Do not reintroduce
# either to lower the flag count.
#
# FORMAT (case-block, because a count-vs-structure case is irreducibly multi-line):
#   --- <EXPECT> <CLASS> <label>
#   <literal block content, one or more lines>
#   --- END
# where
#   <EXPECT> = FLAG      the predicate MUST flag this block
#            | CLEAN     the predicate MUST examine this block and MUST NOT flag it
#            | SCOPE-OUT the predicate MUST examine ZERO pairs in this block
#   <CLASS>  = COUNT     a stated cardinality against its adjacent enumeration
#
# A CLEAN case that examines zero pairs is a FAILURE, not a pass. That is the whole
# point of the SCOPE-OUT expectation existing as a separate verdict: "not flagged"
# and "not examined" are different results and this harness refuses to conflate them.
#
# Arms: 2 FLAG · 3 CLEAN · 2 SCOPE-OUT — 7 cases total.

--- FLAG COUNT probe-validity-coverage-boundary-defect
COVERED — 11 of the 12 observed shapes, across these classes:

- wrong denominator
- truncated extraction
- empty extraction
- non-discriminating predicate
- wrong scope
- zero-byte control
- no-probe-at-all
- wrong pattern in the false-alarm direction
--- END

--- END

# The two cases below are the VERBATIM inline originals from
# core/hooks/testdata/count-structure-fixtures.txt. They pin the declared v1 boundary:
# an inline semicolon-delimited enumeration is NOT examined, because that form's own
# false-positive surface has not been measured and shipping it unmeasured is the defect
# this check exists to prevent. When the inline form graduates, these two rows flip
# from SCOPE-OUT to FLAG and CLEAN respectively and this file is their regression set.

--- SCOPE-OUT COUNT inline-original-flag-arm
COVERED (11 of the 12 observed shapes): wrong denominator; truncated extraction; empty extraction; non-discriminating predicate; wrong scope; zero-byte control; no-probe-at-all; wrong pattern in the false-alarm direction.
--- END

--- SCOPE-OUT COUNT inline-original-clean-arm
COVERED - 11 of the 12 observed shapes, across 6 classes: wrong-denominator (2 shapes); truncated-or-empty-extraction (4); non-discriminating-predicate (2); wrong-scope (1); no-probe (1); wrong-pattern-false-alarm (1).
--- END
